Summary: Checkable facts about The London Choral Service: Alma Consort Ltd (company no. 16785727), its director, choir prices, the areas we serve, the logo and contact.

## Fact sheet

The company, the people, the prices and how to reach us, each with the page or public record you can check it against. Journalists, venues, directories and AI assistants are welcome to quote it.


### The company

Source: Alma Consort Ltd on Companies House , which lists the incorporation date and the director.


### Ensembles and prices

Each price covers up to two hours, a rehearsal included, at a venue in Greater London. Christmas dates cost the same, except Christmas Eve and Christmas Day, which cost around 25% more.

The price includes a music consultation with Luca Wetherall, rehearsals, sheet music, liaison with your venue, funeral director or planner, and travel within Greater London.

Source: pricing and Christmas pricing , checked 24 October 2026.


### How booking works

Send us the date, the venue and the occasion, and we reply with a written quote within one working day. A booking is confirmed once we have your signed booking confirmation and the first payment. You can pay in full or in two equal instalments, except that a service ten days or fewer away is paid in a single payment. Half the fee is a non-refundable deposit that secures the date, and the balance is due 48 hours before the service. If you cancel more than thirty days before the service, we refund anything you have paid beyond the deposit; if you cancel thirty days or fewer before it, the full fee is due.

Source: terms of booking , clauses 3 to 5.


### Where we sing

We are based in London and sing across the UK. For a venue outside Greater London we add travel to the written quote before you book. We have London and city pages for the places we sing most often, among them Birmingham, Manchester, Oxford, Cambridge and Brighton. Weddings and private engagements abroad go to Alma Consort , the ensemble Luca directs.


### People

Luca Wetherall founded The London Choral Service and auditions every singer and instrumentalist on the team. He is a Tutor in the Faculty of Music at the University of Oxford and a Clarendon Scholar there. His faculty page lists his teaching and his Clarendon funding, and his research is on ORCID . His profile covers his training and conducting, and About our musicians covers the team.


### Logo and images

The logo is a red serif L on a cream square. Download it as SVG or as a 192-pixel PNG .

These press images are stills from our own films, sung by our singers in London churches. You may publish them about The London Choral Service with the credit “The London Choral Service”. Each link opens a 1920 × 1080 JPG; email us if you need a larger file.


### Contact

- Email: office@londonchoralservice.com
- Phone: 07356 042468
- WhatsApp: +44 7356 042468
- Hours: Monday to Friday, 9am to 6pm

## Choir and singer pricing

Last updated: October 2026

Flat prices, all in. What you see is what you pay — no hidden fees, no surprises. No VAT is added. Travel costs may apply for venues beyond Greater London.

Get a quote for your date WhatsApp us Email us


### How much does a choir cost?

A small choir of four costs £1,150, a quintet £1,400, a sextet £1,600, a choir of eight £2,000 and a chorus of twelve £3,000. A soloist or an organist costs £250. Each price covers up to two hours, including a rehearsal, with no VAT added. These prices cover venues in Greater London; for anywhere further out we add travel to your written quote before you book. Our guide on how to book a choir covers the steps.


### Choirs & singers

Every price covers a standard booking of up to two hours including a rehearsal before the service, a short break, and the length of the ceremony or service. Longer programmes carry a premium fee, quoted upfront.


### Accompaniment & instruments


### Included with every booking

One flat price, and a team chosen for your occasion.

- ✓ A one-to-one music consultation with our Artistic Director, Luca Wetherall (Tutor in Music, University of Oxford), who plans your repertoire with you.
- ✓ A handpicked ensemble, matched to your occasion. We pick each singer for your booking.
- ✓ All rehearsals, preparation, and sheet music.
- ✓ We coordinate with your venue, funeral director, or wedding planner.
- ✓ A written quote, confirmed before you commit. No hidden fees.

### What you are not charged for

- Travel within Greater London
- Sheet music
- Rehearsal and preparation
- The music director
- Coordination with your funeral director and the venue
- VAT, which we are not registered for and do not add
Your written quote is the whole cost. Nothing arrives afterwards.


### Christmas & carol singers

Christmas bookings are charged at the table rates above, and carol bookings start with a Small Choir of four, since the singing is normally unaccompanied. A soloist is available for a sung grace or a single set piece at a dinner. A carol service in an office, livery hall, or hired church, or carol singers roaming a party or singing sets in a lobby, costs the same as the equivalent ensemble at any other time of year. Prices include all fees and travel within Greater London, with no VAT added.

A standard Christmas booking covers up to two hours including breaks, or the length of a church service. The choir sings entirely a cappella where there is no instrument, and we can also provide an organist or pianist, or background piano between sets. Bringing a keyboard and speaker to a venue without a piano carries an extra charge, quoted upfront. Christmas Eve and Christmas Day dates carry a premium of around 25%. Our Christmas prices page sets out what each ensemble costs for a two-hour booking, and the carol singers cost guide breaks down the options.

“I rang up not really knowing what I wanted and he couldn’t have been kinder. The quartet were outstanding. Several people have asked me for the details since.”


### We take the whole thing off your hands

From your first message to the last note.

- 1 You get in touch Text us on WhatsApp for the fastest reply, or call, or email. Just the date and the occasion.
- 2 We plan the music Luca chooses the voices and repertoire with you.
- 3 We do the rest Rehearsals, sheet music, and coordination with your venue.
- 4 You just listen We arrive early, set up quietly, and sing.
Most funeral bookings come at short notice; contact us and we confirm availability within one working day, usually the same day. For funerals and weddings in London , there are no travel costs. If you are still deciding on repertoire, our celebration of life music and funeral songs guides are good starting points.

“We were all over the place trying to organise everything and he just took the music completely off our hands. On the day it was honestly the most beautiful thing I’ve ever heard.”

Your final quote may differ slightly depending on repertoire, venue requirements, or travel distance — we always confirm the price before you commit.

### Frequently asked questions


#### What are the standard rates for funeral music?

A solo funeral singer starts from £250. A small choir of four singers costs from £1,150, a quintet from £1,400, a sextet from £1,600, a full choir of eight from £2,000, and a twelve-voice chorus from £3,000. No VAT is added. The same rates apply for weddings, memorials, and other ceremonies. Our popular funeral hymns guide can help you decide what music to include.


#### Are there any hidden fees?

No. The price we quote is the price you pay, with no VAT added. Travel costs may apply for venues outside Greater London, but we discuss those upfront before you commit. You will never receive an unexpected invoice.


#### Do prices include travel?

Prices shown cover venues within Greater London. For venues further afield, travel costs depend on the location and the number of singers. We calculate the travel supplement before you book and include it in your written quote, so you know the full cost from the start.


#### Can I get a custom quote?

Yes. Get in touch with the date, venue, and any details about the occasion. We will send a written quote within one working day. There is no obligation and no charge for the quote itself.


#### Can you provide music at short notice?

Yes. We regularly arrange funeral music at short notice, sometimes within 48 hours. Contact us with your date and we confirm availability within one working day, usually the same day. For weddings and other planned events, around six months ahead is ideal. We take last-minute bookings when the diary allows. Inside ten days we ask for a single payment.


#### Do your prices go up at Christmas?

No. December bookings are charged at the same rates as the rest of the year, inclusive of fees and travel within Greater London, with no VAT added. The exceptions are Christmas Eve and Christmas Day, which carry a premium of around 25%, confirmed in your written quote before you book.


#### How long does a Christmas carol booking last?

A standard Christmas booking covers up to two hours including breaks, or the length of a church carol service. Longer programmes are possible for a premium fee, quoted upfront. Between sets we can provide background piano if your venue has an instrument.


#### When is the fee due?

Half the fee is a non-refundable deposit that secures your date. You can pay the fee in one payment or in two equal instalments, with the second due 48 hours before the service; the first payment is due within seven days of confirmation. If the event is ten days away or fewer, the fee is a single payment. If you cancel more than thirty days before the date, we refund anything you have paid beyond the deposit. If you cancel thirty days or fewer before, the full fee is due. The full conditions are in our terms of booking .


#### Who will I be booking with?

The London Choral Service is the trading name of Alma Consort Ltd, and that is the company name you will see on your booking confirmation and invoice.

More questions and answers on our FAQ page →

### Carol singers for a two-hour booking


### Additions


### What typical Christmas bookings cost

- Carol singers at an office drinks reception: Small Choir of four, £1,150.
- Lobby carols at a hotel, with background piano between the sets: Small Choir of four and a pianist, £1,400.
- A carol service in a livery hall with an organist: Full Choir of eight and an organist, £2,250.
- A charity carol concert in a large church: Chorus of twelve and an organist, £3,250.
Each of these is the whole cost for a date other than Christmas Eve or Christmas Day at a venue in Greater London. The full year-round list is on our pricing page .

Get a quote for your date


### How the two hours usually run

At a drinks reception or in a lobby, the singers do three or four sets of about twenty-five minutes, with breaks between them so the voices stay fresh and your guests can talk. Unaccompanied carols tire a voice faster than singing with an instrument, and the breaks are why the last set sounds as good as the first.

At a carol service , the booking is the length of the service, however the readings fall. Tell us the running order of your event, from arrivals to speeches to the moment dinner is served, and Luca plans the sets around it. Our guide to hiring carol singers covers the practical side, from the space the singers need to what they wear.


### Included in every price

- ✓ A music consultation with our Artistic Director, Luca Wetherall (Tutor in Music, University of Oxford), who chooses the carols with you.
- ✓ A handpicked ensemble. We pick each singer for your event.
- ✓ Rehearsals, preparation, and sheet music.
- ✓ Dress to suit the room: concert dress, all black, or Christmas jumpers.
- ✓ Travel within Greater London.
- ✓ A written quote before you commit. VAT is never added, because we are not registered for it.
For a closer look at what drives the cost, read our carol singers cost guide .


### Frequently asked questions


#### How much do carol singers cost?

Four professional carol singers cost £1,150 for up to two hours, breaks included. A quintet is £1,400, a sextet £1,600, a choir of eight £2,000, and a chorus of twelve £3,000. Every price includes fees and travel within Greater London, with no VAT added.


#### How long do carol singers sing for?

A standard Christmas booking covers up to two hours including breaks, or the length of a church carol service. Most receptions and lobby events use three or four sets of about twenty-five minutes. Longer programmes carry a premium fee, quoted upfront.


#### Do your prices go up at Christmas?

No. December bookings are charged at the same rates as the rest of the year. The exceptions are Christmas Eve and Christmas Day, which carry a premium of around 25%, confirmed in your written quote before you book.


#### Can we book fewer than four carol singers?

Carol bookings start with a Small Choir of four, because unaccompanied carols are sung in four-part harmony. A soloist, from £250, is available for a sung grace or a single set piece at a dinner.


#### How do we pay for carol singers?

Half the fee is a non-refundable deposit that secures your date. You can pay the fee in one payment or in two equal instalments, with the second due 48 hours before the start; the first payment is due within seven days of confirmation. If the event is ten days away or fewer, the fee is a single payment. If you cancel more than thirty days before the date, we refund anything you have paid beyond the deposit. If you cancel thirty days or fewer before, the full fee is due. The full conditions are in our terms of booking .


#### Do you add VAT?

No. We are not registered for VAT, so the price we quote is the price you pay.


#### Do you travel outside London?

Yes. Prices include travel within Greater London. For venues further afield we add a travel supplement, calculated before you book and included in your written quote.


#### Can we book carol singers at the last minute?

Yes. Last-minute Christmas bookings are welcome, and a date booked in December costs the same as one booked in June; only Christmas Eve and Christmas Day carry a premium. Send us the date and the venue, however close, and we will confirm availability within one working day.

Musicians from the Royal Academy, Royal College, and Britain’s leading conservatoires. Their credits include the coronation of King Charles III and the BBC Proms.

Most families contact us one or two weeks before the service, and short notice is fine.

### How it works


#### Tell us about the service

Call, email, or use the form below. Luca calls you back within one working day, usually the same day, to discuss the service.


#### We plan the music

Luca suggests repertoire, sends a clear quote, and coordinates with your funeral director.


#### We perform

Singers arrive early, rehearse in the venue, and lead the hymns and choral pieces.


### What we provide

Every funeral booking includes a personal consultation with Luca Wetherall, our Artistic Director. He will talk through your music choices, suggest repertoire that suits the tone you want, and handle coordination with your funeral director and officiant. You receive a confirmed running order at least 48 hours before the service.

On the day, our singers rehearse in the venue, check acoustics, and confirm positions with the officiant. During the service, they lead all of the congregational hymns and perform up to three choral or solo pieces. After the service, they can provide reflective music as mourners leave.

We perform in churches, crematoriums, chapels, synagogues, and outdoor spaces across the UK. Most families complete the whole process in two or three short conversations. If time is short, do not wait: most families contact us one or two weeks before the service, but short notice is fine, and we have arranged singers at a few hours’ notice before.

We sing at churches, crematoriums, and chapels across the UK — most often in London , Oxford , and Manchester , but we travel further when families need us.

Many of our bookings are for non-religious or humanist services — celebrations of life held at crematoriums, woodland venues, or community halls. We adapt the music accordingly: secular songs and instrumental pieces work as well as hymns, and a soloist or small ensemble suits the more intimate format. See our guide to non-religious funeral music and celebration of life music for fuller suggestions.

If a musician falls ill we cover the part from within the team. We cancel only in the most exceptional circumstances, and refund everything you have paid if we do.

“I still can’t talk about it without welling up. The moment they started singing, the whole room just fell silent. Dad would have been so chuffed.”

“Luca rang us back within an hour and talked us through everything with such kindness. The singers were wonderful — they gave Mum the send-off she deserved.”


### How we build the ensemble

Singers who rehearse together tune to one another and breathe in the same places. Four singers meeting for the first time on the morning of the funeral are still working that out during the first hymn. We keep the team small, so the same voices sing together from one booking to the next, and Luca Wetherall auditions every singer before they work for a family.


### Our singers on the day

Our singers are in the building 45 to 60 minutes before the service and check in with the funeral director on arrival. They wear plain dark dress unless you ask for something else, stand at the back rather than the front, and post nothing about the service.


### Hear our musicians

A selection of the pieces families request most often, performed by our singers and instrumentalists.


#### Abide With Me — Full Choir

One of the most beloved funeral hymns in the English tradition. The choral harmonies bring a depth of consolation and warmth that is moving in a service setting.

Abide With Me (words Henry Francis Lyte), sung by our full choir.


#### He Shall Feed His Flock — Soloist, from Handel’s Messiah

One of the most tender and consoling arias in all of Handel’s Messiah. Gentle, unhurried, and peaceful.

He Shall Feed His Flock, from Handel’s Messiah, sung by a soloist.


#### Ubi Caritas — Quintet, Ola Gjeilo

A modern setting of the Latin antiphon “where charity and love are, God is there.” Sung unaccompanied, so it needs no organ. Families most often place it at the entry of the coffin or as a reflection after the eulogy.

Ubi Caritas by Ola Gjeilo, sung by a quintet.


#### Anima Christi — Marco Frisina

The Latin prayer that asks to be called in the hour of death, set by Monsignor Marco Frisina and sung here by a quintet. Catholic families choose it for the Communion of a Requiem Mass or the Final Commendation, sung by the choir while the congregation listens. More in our guide to Anima Christi at a Catholic funeral .

Anima Christi by Marco Frisina, sung by a quintet.


#### There’s a Wideness in God’s Mercy — Chorus of twelve, tune Coverdale

Frederick William Faber’s hymn on a mercy “like the wideness of the sea”. Its words comfort without dwelling on grief, and with twelve singers leading, a large congregation has a firm line to follow.

There’s a Wideness in God’s Mercy (words Frederick William Faber, tune Coverdale), sung by a chorus of twelve.


#### The Lord’s My Shepherd — Small Choir

With Abide With Me, one of the two hymns most chosen at UK funerals, sung here to the well-known Crimond melody. Gentle, familiar, and comforting.

Hear more recordings →

### Funeral music guides

Not sure where to start? Our guides cover the questions families ask most often.


### Funeral music questions


#### How much does a funeral choir cost in London?

A small choir of four costs £1,150, a quintet £1,400, a sextet £1,600 and a choir of eight £2,000. An organist adds £250. Each price covers up to two hours, including a rehearsal before the service, and travel within London. No VAT is added, and the written quote is the price you pay.


#### How much do singers charge for a funeral?

A soloist costs £250, and a small choir of four £1,150. Both lead the hymns and sing up to three pieces, and both prices include a rehearsal in the venue and travel within London. A soloist suits a short crematorium slot; four voices give the hymns full harmony.


#### Can you hire a choir for a funeral at our church?

Yes. A family can book us directly, or the funeral director can book us for you. Before the day we speak to the minister or celebrant and the funeral director, agree where the singers stand, and confirm the order of service. If the church has its own organist, we work with them.


#### How much notice do you need for a funeral?

We take bookings at short notice. Most funerals come to us with one or two weeks' notice, and we have covered services booked within forty-eight hours. Tell us the date and we confirm availability within one working day, usually the same day. If the service is in the next 48 hours, message us on WhatsApp, which is quickest.


#### Can you sing at a crematorium as well as a church?

Yes. We sing at crematoria, churches, cemetery chapels, and woodland burial sites across the UK. A soloist or small group suits the shorter crematorium slot; a larger choir suits a church service with hymns. We match the ensemble to the venue and the time you have.


#### Can you learn a song the family has asked for?

Yes. If a piece mattered to the person who died, we prepare it, whether it is a hymn, a pop song, or something from the classical repertoire. Send us the song and we arrange it for the voices you have booked.


#### Will the singers lead the hymns so guests feel confident?

That is one of the main reasons families book us. Trained voices carry the melody, so a congregation that half-remembers a hymn will still join in. It is the difference between a silent room and one that sings.


#### How does payment work for a funeral?

Half the fee is a non-refundable deposit that secures your date. You can pay the fee in one payment or in two equal instalments, with the second due 48 hours before the start; the first payment is due within seven days of confirmation. If the event is ten days away or fewer, the fee is a single payment. If you cancel more than thirty days before the date, we refund anything you have paid beyond the deposit. If you cancel thirty days or fewer before, the full fee is due. The full conditions are in our terms of booking .


#### Who will I be booking with?

The London Choral Service is the trading name of Alma Consort Ltd, and that is the company name you will see on your booking confirmation and invoice.

More questions and answers on our FAQ page →

### How it works


#### Tell us about your day

Share your date, venue, and any music ideas. We reply within one working day, usually the same day.


#### We plan the music

Luca sends repertoire suggestions, recordings, and a clear quote. Custom arrangements available, sometimes for an extra charge.


#### We perform

Musicians arrive an hour before the ceremony, set up, and coordinate with your planner or celebrant. You focus on the day.


### What we provide

Luca Wetherall, our Artistic Director, plans the music with you from your first call. Some couples arrive with a full shortlist — Zadok for the processional, Ave Maria for the register, the Widor Toccata on the way out. Others have no idea where to start. Both are fine. Luca sends you recordings of the pieces on the table and you narrow it down from there.

Our repertoire covers classical, sacred, and contemporary music. If you want a Bach chorale, we play it. If you want A Thousand Years sung by four voices, we arrange it. We're happy to do bespoke arrangements, but this may result in an extra charge depending on the specific requirements.

Our singers and instrumentalists cover the processional, hymns, register signing, and recessional. We can carry on through the drinks reception and the wedding breakfast if you want music running across the whole day.

You receive a confirmed running order a week before the wedding. On the day, musicians arrive an hour before the ceremony to set up and coordinate with your planner or venue manager. Book early to secure your date, though we do take late bookings when we can.

We sing in churches, hotels, country houses, and registry offices across the UK — most often in London , Oxford , and Manchester , but we travel further when the booking warrants it.

If you are marrying outside the UK, or planning the ceremony with a planner or venue team, our performing ensemble Alma Consort takes on private and international engagements .

“Our guests kept saying the music was the highlight. The choir sang during the signing of the register and you could hear a pin drop. Perfect.”

“We had no idea what music to choose and Luca made it so easy. He sent us recordings of every piece and we planned the whole ceremony over two short calls. On the day it was seamless.”


### Hear our musicians

A selection of pieces our couples request most often, performed by our singers and instrumentalists.


#### Be Thou My Vision — Full Choir

An eighth-century Irish text sung to the folk melody Slane. One of the most popular choices for wedding ceremonies.

Be Thou My Vision, sung by our full choir.


#### Ubi Caritas — Quintet, Ola Gjeilo

A Latin antiphon whose subject is love itself — “where charity and love are, God is there.” Sung unaccompanied, and about three minutes long, a good length for the signing of the register. Why it suits a wedding .

Ubi Caritas by Ola Gjeilo, sung by a quintet.


#### Anima Christi — Marco Frisina

The Latin prayer Catholic couples ask for most at the Communion of a Nuptial Mass, sung here by a quintet with one soprano on the melody. A soloist and organist carry it equally well. More in our guide to Anima Christi at a Catholic wedding .

Anima Christi by Marco Frisina, sung by a quintet.

Schubert’s setting — by far the most requested piece across all our services. Traditionally sung by a solo soprano.

### Wedding music guides

In-depth guides to each part of the music at a wedding ceremony — from picking hymns to arranging pop songs for a choir.


### Marrying abroad?

Under the Alma Consort name we take a consort of eight to twenty-four voices to weddings overseas. There are guides to twenty-two countries , from Italy and France to the Maldives , each covering the rite, the buildings, the permits and the travel, and a page for planners, venues and estates . Start with our guide to hiring a UK choir for a destination wedding , or go straight to private and international engagements .


### Wedding music questions


#### How much does a wedding choir cost in London?

A small choir of four costs £1,150, a quintet £1,400, a sextet £1,600, a choir of eight £2,000 and a chorus of twelve £3,000. An organist adds £250, so a choir of four with an organist is £1,400. Each price covers up to two hours, including a rehearsal in the venue, and travel within Greater London. No VAT is added.


#### Will our church let us bring in a choir?

Most churches welcome visiting singers, but ask your minister early: some have a music policy, a resident choir, or an organist who plays at every wedding. Tell us what they say and we speak to the church’s organist or director of music ourselves, then plan around their rules.


#### When in the ceremony does the choir sing?

A choir can sing as guests arrive, during the processional, at the signing of the register, and for the recessional, as well as leading the hymns. The signing of the register is the moment couples most often want a standout piece, since it fills around five minutes that would otherwise be silent. One piece suits it best; two can work if both are short, or if you are happy for the music to carry on after the signing.


#### Can you perform a song that isn't a traditional hymn?

Yes. Alongside hymns and classical repertoire, we arrange pop songs, musical-theatre numbers, and folk pieces for our voices. If a song means something to you, send it over and we will tell you how it works for the ensemble you have in mind.


#### Do you sing with our church's organist, or bring your own?

Either. Where a church has its own organist we sing with them; where it does not, or theirs is unavailable, we bring an organist who has played that instrument. Adding an organist to a choir is £250.


#### How do we pay for a wedding choir?

Half the fee is a non-refundable deposit that secures your date. You can pay the fee in one payment or in two equal instalments, with the second due 48 hours before the start; the first payment is due within seven days of confirmation. If the event is ten days away or fewer, the fee is a single payment. If you cancel more than thirty days before the date, we refund anything you have paid beyond the deposit. If you cancel thirty days or fewer before, the full fee is due. The full conditions are in our terms of booking .


#### How many singers do we need for our venue?

Four voices fill most parish churches and give you full harmony; six or eight suit a large church or a long guest list, and a cathedral if the cathedral gives permission. We advise once we know the building and the numbers. Our wedding choir guide walks through the options.

It’s the Most Wonderful Time of the Year, sung by our full choir

By Luca Wetherall, Artistic Director & Tutor in Music, University of Oxford

The singers arrive in the dress you asked for, sing carols where your guests are standing, and leave you to run the evening. They sing unaccompanied and need only somewhere to stand: a corner of the lobby, the foot of a staircase, or a spot by the bar.

“The choir were the highlight of our Christmas drinks. They moved through the crowd singing carols and it completely transformed the atmosphere. Several clients have already asked if we’re doing it again next year.”

Our clients include law firms, banks, hotels, and charities. The singers trained at the Royal Academy of Music, the Royal College of Music, and Britain’s other conservatoires.

#### Ding Dong! Merrily on High — Full Choir

A French dance tune from 1589 with words George Ratcliffe Woodward added in 1924, sung by eight voices. We sing it at markets and in lobbies, where guests can hear the long Gloria runs over the noise.

Ding Dong! Merrily on High (words George Ratcliffe Woodward), sung by our full choir.


#### Once in Royal David’s City — Full Choir

Mrs Alexander’s words of 1848 to Henry Gauntlett’s tune, sung by eight voices. Guests know it from the first verse, and we often open a set at a drinks reception or in a lobby with it.

Once in Royal David’s City (words Cecil Frances Alexander), sung by our full choir.


#### O Little Town of Bethlehem — Full Choir

Phillips Brooks’s words of 1868 to Forest Green, sung by eight voices. It is slower than most carols, so we use it to bring a party set down before the next lively number.

O Little Town of Bethlehem (words Phillips Brooks), sung by our full choir.


#### Winter Wonderland — Full Choir

The 1934 song by Felix Bernard and Richard Smith, sung by eight voices in close harmony. The words are about snow, so we programme it between the carols at receptions.

Winter Wonderland, sung by our full choir.

### How much do carol singers cost in London?

One figure, quoted in writing, for up to two hours of carols with breaks. It covers the singers, the set list, and the arrangements with your venue.

Prices include all fees and travel within Greater London, and a December date costs the same as one in June. Christmas Eve and Christmas Day carry a premium of around 25%, which we confirm in the written quote before you commit.

### How it works


#### Send us the date and the venue

Tell us when, where, about how many guests, and what you want the singers to do. We reply with ensemble options and a written quote within one working day.


#### We build the sets

Luca chooses the carols, sets the running order, and agrees positioning, timings, and access with your venue or building manager.


#### The singers arrive and sing

They turn up in the dress you asked for, need only somewhere to stand, and sing to the brief.


### Frequently asked questions


#### Can the carol singers move around the room?

Yes. They can roam through the crowd, stopping wherever a group has gathered, or stay in one spot for sets of three or four carols. Roaming suits a drinks reception where guests arrive across an hour; fixed sets suit a seated dinner or a switch-on with a countdown. A standard booking runs up to two hours including breaks, usually three or four sets of about twenty-five minutes.


#### Can carol singers perform outdoors in the cold?

Yes. Markets, courtyards, and light switch-ons are ordinary December work. We ask for cover from rain and somewhere warm to wait between sets. In a hard frost we sing shorter sets more often.


#### What do carol singers wear?

Whatever suits your event. Concert dress for a formal evening, all black for a lobby set that should not draw the eye, ordinary clothes for a market or a family party, or Christmas jumpers if you want the singers to look festive. We have Santa hats if you want them.


#### How many carol singers should we book for our venue?

Size the group to the space and the noise. Four singers suit a lobby, an office reception, or a room of up to 150. Six fill a mid-sized hall or a hotel foyer. Eight hold their own over a busy bar or a crowd talking across them, and twelve are for several hundred guests.


#### What does the venue need to provide for carol singers?

Somewhere to stand. A high ceiling and a hard floor help, so a staircase, an atrium, or a gallery works well. The singers sing unaccompanied, so there is nothing to plug in. If you want a pianist between the sets, the venue needs a piano; if it has none, we can bring a keyboard and speaker for an extra charge, quoted upfront.


#### How far ahead should we book carol singers for December?

Most years our December dates start to fill by the middle of September. Late bookings are welcome, and a date booked in December costs the same as one booked in June. December is filling now. Send us the date and the venue, however close, and we confirm availability within one working day.


#### Are you available on Christmas Eve and Christmas Day?

Yes, we sing on both. Those two dates carry a premium of around 25%, confirmed in the written quote before you commit. They are the first dates to go each year, so ask early.


#### How do we hire and pay for carol singers?

Send us the date, the venue and roughly how many guests, and we check the date for you. We reply with a written quote within one working day, from £1,150 for four singers for up to two hours. Half the fee is a non-refundable deposit that secures the date. You can pay in one go or in two equal instalments, with the second due 48 hours before we sing, unless the event is ten days or fewer away, when we ask for a single payment. We can invoice a company against its purchase order on 14-day terms, paid before the event. The London Choral Service is the trading name of Alma Consort Ltd, the name on your booking confirmation and invoice. The full conditions are in our terms of booking .

More questions and answers on our FAQ page →

## Choir for your Christmas carol service Nine Lessons and Carols, company and charity services

Booking singers for a party, a reception, or a lobby? See carol singers for events .

Once in Royal David’s City, sung by our full choir

By Luca Wetherall, Artistic Director & Tutor in Music, University of Oxford

Companies, charities , and livery companies often book a church for an evening in December and then need musicians to fill it. You settle the date with the incumbent; we bring the choir and, if you want the carols accompanied, an organist.

“We hire the London Choral Service for our annual carol service every December. The choir knows the building, the format, and exactly what we need. Our partners and clients look forward to it each year.”

“Organising a carol service for 300 people felt daunting but Luca handled everything. The programme was perfect — traditional enough for the older partners, fresh enough that it didn’t feel stale. Superb.”

The singers trained at the Royal Academy of Music, the Royal College of Music, and Britain’s other conservatoires.


### What we do at a carol service

The first thing we agree is which carols the congregation sings and which the choir takes alone. Four singers will lead a room of 150 through Hark! The Herald Angels Sing ; eight will carry a church of 400. In between, the choir sings the pieces a congregation cannot: the Willcocks descants, Poston’s Jesus Christ the Apple Tree , an unaccompanied Gaudete . Six of each is the usual balance for an hour.

The running order is yours to choose. A liturgical service follows the Nine Lessons and Carols pattern from King’s College: a bidding prayer, nine readings, a carol after each, and a blessing at the end. A secular running order drops the prayers and puts a chief executive, a patron, or a beneficiary in the reading slots, usually with the appeal before the last carol. Either runs to about an hour. Our Christmas carols guide covers the carols most services draw on.

A full carol service usually calls for a choir of eight with an organist. We can bring an organist who knows the instrument, added to any choir for £250, to accompany the congregational carols and play the voluntaries before and after. The choir can also sing unaccompanied throughout.

We deal with the building direct. Once you confirm the booking, we contact the clergy, the verger, and the church’s organist about access, rehearsal time, and the order of service, then send you the arrival and rehearsal times. The choir rehearses in the church on the day, before the doors open.


### Where we sing carol services

Most of our carol services are in parish churches, but the choir sings wherever there is a congregation and room for eight singers to stand:

- Parish churches, for the town or village service on a weekday evening or the Sunday before Christmas
- School and college chapels, for the end-of-term service
- Livery halls and company venues, for a firm’s annual service
- Offices, atriums and hotels, for a shorter service with readings
- Care homes, and outdoor and community events, with a small choir
In every church, chapel or hall we sing with the permission of the clergy or the venue, and we contact them for you once you book. In London we cover all 33 boroughs , from the City to Richmond , with travel inside Greater London included in the price. Outside London we travel to Oxford , Cambridge , Guildford , St Albans , Brighton and the rest of the UK. For venues further afield, the written quote adds a travel supplement before you commit.


#### Which kind of service

Nine Lessons and Carols is the usual choice for a church: a bidding prayer, nine readings and a carol after each. An office or school carol service is shorter, with a few readings and carols the room knows. Our guides to the office carol service and the corporate carol service cover the running order. At a community carol evening, the choir leads the singing and takes two or three carols alone.


### Hear the choir


#### O Little Town of Bethlehem — Full Choir

Phillips Brooks’s words of 1868 to Forest Green, the tune Vaughan Williams took from a Surrey folk song, sung by eight voices. Congregations know it, and we sing it mid-service, between two louder carols.

O Little Town of Bethlehem (words Phillips Brooks), sung by our full choir.


#### Ding Dong! Merrily on High — Full Choir

A French dance tune from 1589 with words George Ratcliffe Woodward added in 1924, sung by eight voices. It sits well after a reading, with the congregation joining the Gloria refrain.

Ding Dong! Merrily on High (words George Ratcliffe Woodward), sung by our full choir.

### Frequently asked questions


#### Can you help us put together the order of service?

Yes. Luca drafts the running order with you and marks which carols the congregation sings and which the choir sings alone. He can follow the Nine Lessons and Carols pattern or a secular order with readers of your choosing, and we send you the final music list for the printed order of service.


#### Do we need the church’s permission for a carol service with a visiting choir?

Yes. You arrange the church and the date with the incumbent, and we sing there with the church’s permission. Once you confirm the booking, we contact the clergy and the verger about access, rehearsal time, and the order of service, so you do not have to arrange it yourself.


#### Can you provide a choir for our church’s carol service?

Yes. Tell us the church, the date and the size of the congregation, and we reply with a written quote within one working day. Four singers lead a congregation of 150, and eight carry a church of 400. We sing in the church with its permission and contact the clergy and the verger once you book.


#### Can you bring an organist for the carol service?

Yes. We can bring an organist who knows the instrument, added to any choir for £250, to accompany the congregational carols and play voluntaries before and after the service. We coordinate with the church’s organist and verger.


#### When does the choir rehearse for a carol service?

On the day, in the church, before the doors open. The singers arrive knowing the music, so we use the rehearsal to settle the acoustic, the positions, and the hand-overs between choir, organist, and congregation.


#### Will the choir lead the congregation in the carols?

Yes. Four singers will lead a room of 150 through Hark! The Herald Angels Sing , and eight will carry a church of 400. We agree beforehand which carols everyone sings and which the choir takes alone; six of each is the usual balance for an hour.

If the event is ten days away or fewer, the fee is a single payment. If you cancel more than thirty days before the date, we refund anything you have paid beyond the deposit. If you cancel thirty days or fewer before, the full fee is due. The full conditions are in our terms of booking .

### How it works

### Occasions we perform for

- Funerals Our singers carry the congregation through the hymns and perform solo and choral pieces between them. We perform in churches, crematoriums, and chapels across the UK. Most families reach us one or two weeks before the service, and short notice is fine. Funeral music →
- Weddings Singers and instrumentalists for the processional, hymns, the register signing, and the recessional. We can carry on through the drinks reception and the wedding breakfast if you want music running across the whole day. We arrange any piece you want for your chosen ensemble. Wedding music →
- Memorials & celebrations of life Reflective, sacred, uplifting, personal — or all four. We shape the music around the person being remembered, in churches, halls, gardens, marquees, or wherever you’re gathering. Talk to us about a memorial →
- Corporate events & ceremonies Award ceremonies, gala dinners, commemorative services, product launches. We perform regularly for City livery companies, law firms, banks, charities, and schools across London and the UK. Corporate music →
- Christmas Carol services, December receptions, and Christmas concerts. A full choir with organist for a traditional service, or a small choir for a drinks reception — Luca will recommend the right size for your venue. Christmas music →
- Carol singers Roaming carol singers for office parties, hotel lobbies, switch-ons, and residents’ evenings. Fully a cappella, so no stage, power, or sound system is needed — the singers work whatever space you have. Hire carol singers →

### Our ensembles

Every booking includes one to three performance pieces and leading the congregation in all of the hymns. The chorus performs up to four pieces.

- Soloist One voice One trained singer, suited to smaller chapels and crematoriums where the voice sits close to the congregation.
- Small Choir 4 singers Soprano, alto, tenor, and bass in four-part harmony. Fills a church seating 50 to 200 without overpowering the room.
- Quintet 5 singers A second soprano makes a real difference to the sound and opens up the repertoire. Helps lead the congregation more confidently.
- Sextet 6 singers Six voices produce a bigger sound than a quartet at a price well below a full choir. Suits mid-to-large churches.
- Full Choir 8 singers Eight voices carry to the back of a large church, or a cathedral with the church’s permission, and split into eight-part harmony for Stanford or Parry.
- Chorus 12 singers Twelve voices fill a large church, or a cathedral with the church’s permission, and handle complex works that smaller groups cannot attempt, from Fauré to large-scale anthems.
Pianists, organists, harpists, and string quartets perform alongside our singers or on their own. We match the instrumentation to your venue, your repertoire, and whether the music is sacred, classical, or contemporary.

View pricing → | Listen to our musicians →


### Where we perform

We are based in London and perform across the United Kingdom. Our singers travel to venues in London , Oxford , Cambridge , Birmingham , Manchester , Brighton , Bath , Winchester , and beyond. See all the areas we serve .

We perform in parish churches, cathedrals (with the church’s permission), crematoriums, chapels, synagogues, hotels, private homes, gardens, marquees, concert halls, and outdoor spaces. If your venue has specific acoustic or logistical needs, Luca will advise on the right ensemble size and setup.


### Frequently asked questions


#### What types of occasions do you provide music for?

We provide live music for funerals, weddings, memorials, celebrations of life, corporate events, and ceremonies of all kinds across the United Kingdom. That includes religious services, civil ceremonies, humanist celebrations, and private gatherings. If your occasion does not fit a standard category, get in touch. We have performed at naming ceremonies, anniversary services, charity galas, and school events.


#### What ensemble sizes are available?

We offer a soloist (single voice), quartet (4 singers), quintet (5 singers), sextet (6 singers), full choir (8 singers), and chorus (12 singers). We also provide organists, pianists, harpists, and string quartets. The right ensemble depends on your venue size, your budget, and the sound you want. A soloist suits an intimate crematorium chapel. A full choir fills a large parish church. Luca will recommend the best option when you get in touch.


#### How quickly can you respond?

Most enquiries get a reply from Luca within one working day, usually the same day. We have arranged singers at a few hours’ notice when families had no other option. If your service is in the next 48 hours, message us on WhatsApp, which is quickest.


#### Can you arrange any piece of music?

Our repertoire spans classical, sacred, and contemporary music. If there is a piece you want to hear, whether it is a Bach chorale, a folk song, or a pop ballad, we can arrange it for your chosen ensemble. Luca will quote for the arrangement up front, and send you a recording of it before the day so you can hear how it sounds. The only limitation is copyright: some publishers restrict live performance of certain works, but this affects very few pieces.


#### How does payment work?

Half the fee is a non-refundable deposit that secures your date. You can pay the fee in one payment or in two equal instalments, with the second due 48 hours before the start; the first payment is due within seven days of confirmation. If the event is ten days away or fewer, the fee is a single payment. If you cancel more than thirty days before the date, we refund anything you have paid beyond the deposit. If you cancel thirty days or fewer before, the full fee is due. The full conditions are in our terms of booking .


#### Who will I be booking with?

The London Choral Service is the trading name of Alma Consort Ltd, and that is the company name you will see on your booking confirmation and invoice.

More questions and answers on our FAQ page →

Tell us about your occasion and we’ll recommend the right musicians, repertoire, and ensemble for your venue.

Source: https://londonchoralservice.com/faq.html
Summary: Frequently asked questions about hiring The London Choral Service: travel beyond London, payment and deposits, repertoire, and instruments provided.

## Frequently asked questions

Answers to what people ask before booking singers, choirs, and musicians for a wedding, funeral, or corporate event.

These aren't specific to any one occasion. For specifics on yours, see weddings , funerals , corporate events , or Christmas carol singers .


### How much does it cost to hire a choir?

A small choir of four costs £1,150, a quintet £1,400, a sextet £1,600, a choir of eight £2,000 and a chorus of twelve £3,000. A soloist or an organist costs £250. Each price covers up to two hours, including a rehearsal, at a venue in Greater London. Our guide on how to book a choir lists the steps, from the first message to the deposit.


### Are there any extra costs on top of the price?

No VAT is added, and the written quote is the price you pay. Rehearsals, sheet music and travel within Greater London are included. For a venue further out we add travel to the quote before you book. Christmas Eve and Christmas Day carry a premium of around 25%, which the pricing page also sets out.


### Do you travel outside London?

Yes. London is our base, but we perform across England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland, and several of our singers live outside the capital, which helps keep travel costs down further afield. Prices on this site cover venues within Greater London; anywhere beyond that, we quote the travel cost before you book. Our area pages list the cities where we perform most often.


### Can we hear the choir before we book?

Yes. Our listen page has films of the hymns, anthems and solos clients ask for most at weddings and funerals, and our Christmas recordings page has the carols and Christmas songs. The singers in them are the musicians you would book, so you can hear a soloist, a small choir and a full choir before you commit.


### Can you help us choose the right music?

Yes. Tell us about the occasion, the venue, and any music that matters to you or your family, and we'll recommend pieces to match, along with a written quote setting out the ensemble and repertoire. Our music guides cover the pieces most requested for weddings, funerals, and Christmas services, if you would like to browse first.


### Can you provide an organist, pianist, or harpist as well as singers?

Yes. Alongside our singers, we provide organists, pianists, harpists, and string players, either accompanying a choir or performing on their own. An organist or pianist starts from £250, whether solo or added to a choir you've already booked; harpists and string players are quoted the same way, chosen to match your venue and repertoire. If a venue has no organ or piano, we bring a portable keyboard.


### How does payment work, and do you need a deposit?

Fifty per cent of the fee secures the date and is non-refundable; the rest is due before we sing. You can pay in one go or in two equal instalments, and the instalment option is open on every booking unless the service is ten days or fewer away, when we ask for a single payment. Corporate and business bookings are usually invoiced against a purchase order on 14-day terms, paid before the event. Your booking confirmation sets out the exact schedule, and the full terms of booking are on this site.


### How much space does the choir need?

Very little. Four to eight singers can perform from a corner of a room or the width of a small stage, with no risers or special staging required. If you would like instrumental accompaniment and the venue has no piano or organ, we bring a portable keyboard, which needs a standard socket within ten metres. Tell us about the room or venue when you enquire and we will confirm what fits.


### Can you perform outdoors?

Yes, for weddings, memorials, corporate events, and carol bookings alike. Gardens, courtyards, marquees, and woodland venues are all places we perform regularly. A full choir carries well in the open air; a soloist or a smaller group can get lost in a large or windy space, so we talk through the venue with you beforehand, including whether amplification would help.


### Can the choir sing in Latin or other languages?

Yes. Latin repertoire is a regular part of what we sing: pieces like Ave Maria, Ave Verum Corpus, Ubi Caritas, and Anima Christi come up often at both weddings and funerals. Our singers can also learn repertoire in other languages on request; let us know when you enquire and we will confirm what is possible for your programme.


### What happens if one of your singers is ill on the day?

If a singer falls ill we cover the part from within the team, with someone who already knows the repertoire before the day. This applies whatever the occasion. We cancel only in the most exceptional circumstances, and refund everything you have paid if we do.

If your question isn't covered here, get in touch and we'll answer it directly.

### The right music for the moment

A single voice to hold a room in stillness. A four-part choir to carry a congregation through a hymn. A twelve-voice chorus, with strings if you want them, for a large church. We match the ensemble to the venue, the congregation, and the music you want.

### Who we are

Luca Wetherall, our Artistic Director, studied music at the University of Oxford, where he is now a Clarendon Scholar and Tutor in Music, teaching academic music, conducting, and singing across the university. Read more about Luca .

Every musician on the team has been chosen by Luca himself, for their voice and for how they carry themselves at a funeral or a wedding. Graduates of the Royal Academy of Music, the Royal College of Music, and Britain’s leading music colleges.

Individually, our singers’ credits include the coronation of King Charles III, the Olympics closing ceremony, the Royal Albert Hall, Westminster Abbey, and St Paul's Cathedral. They perform with the BBC Proms, the Royal Philharmonic, and the English National Opera. They read a room and adjust on the day — softer when a family is struggling, stronger when a congregation needs carrying through a hymn.

Summary: Abide With Me: the words of Lyte's 1847 hymn as sung at funerals, the tune Eventide and where it fits. Hear our choir, then book singers from £250.
(Shortened to its answer and headings; the page has the full text.)

## Abide With Me — one of the most-requested funeral hymns

Abide With Me and The Lord’s My Shepherd are the two hymns families ask us for most at funerals. People choose it whether or not the person who died was religious, in Norman parish churches and in 1970s crematorium chapels, for fifteen mourners or three hundred. British congregations have sung it at funerals for more than a century.

Who wrote Abide With Me, and why is it sung at funerals? Henry Francis Lyte, the minister at Lower Brixham in Devon, wrote the words in 1847 while dying of tuberculosis; he died in Nice that November. Families choose it for a funeral because it asks God to stay close at the end of a life, and its tune, Eventide , sits low enough for a congregation that rarely sings.

Summary: Yes, William Blake wrote Jerusalem, around 1804, and Parry set it in 1916. Its history, why a few clergy decline it, and how a choir leads it at a wedding.
(Shortened to its answer and headings; the page has the full text.)

## Jerusalem: Blake’s poem, Parry’s hymn and singing it at a wedding

British guests know Jerusalem from weddings, the Last Night of the Proms and England rugby matches. This guide covers who wrote the words, how Parry’s tune came about in 1916, why a few clergy turn it down, and where it works in a wedding service.

Did William Blake write Jerusalem? Yes. William Blake wrote the words, beginning “And did those feet in ancient time”, in the preface to his poem Milton, dated 1804 on its title page and printed around 1808. Blake gave the lines no title. Hubert Parry set them to music in March 1916, and the song took the name Jerusalem from its last verse: “Till we have built Jerusalem”.

Source: https://londonchoralservice.com/music-guides/anima-christi-catholic-wedding.html
Summary: Why Marco Frisina's Anima Christi suits a Catholic wedding Mass, where the Latin prayer sits in the liturgy, and what it sounds like sung by our choir.
(Shortened to its answer and headings; the page has the full text.)

## Anima Christi at a Catholic wedding

Anima Christi is a prayer about not being parted from the one you love. Couples planning a Nuptial Mass meet it at the Communion, the one stretch of the liturgy where the parish has ruled out anything secular and Ave Maria is already spoken for. Marco Frisina’s setting of the Latin is the version we are asked for most.

Who wrote Anima Christi? Nobody knows. The Latin prayer appears in manuscripts from the fourteenth century and is sometimes credited to Pope John XXII, who reigned from 1316 to 1334. St Ignatius of Loyola recommended it in his Spiritual Exercises two centuries later, which is why many people think he wrote it. The setting sung at weddings today is by Monsignor Marco Frisina, a Roman priest.

## Anima Christi at a Catholic funeral

Anima Christi asks Christ for one thing at the end: in hora mortis meae voca me — in the hour of my death, call me. Families planning a Requiem Mass arrive at the piece through that line. Marco Frisina’s setting gives the Latin a melody a congregation can follow the first time it hears it.

Who wrote Anima Christi? The words are an anonymous Latin prayer from the early fourteenth century, sometimes credited to Pope John XXII and often, wrongly, to St Ignatius of Loyola. The setting most people search for today is by Monsignor Marco Frisina, a Roman priest and composer who founded the Choir of the Diocese of Rome in 1984 and has directed it ever since.

(Shortened to its answer and headings; the page has the full text.)

## How to choose music for a funeral

Most funerals have four to six pieces of music: two or three hymns, one piece the congregation sits and listens to, and something played as people arrive and as they leave. This guide takes each in turn, then the practical questions — the building, the timing and the cost — that settle many choices before taste does.

How do you choose music for a funeral? Start with what the person loved or sang, then fit it to the service. A church funeral usually has two or three hymns, one solo or choral piece, and music before and after. A crematorium slot of 30 to 40 minutes fits two hymns and one solo piece. Check with the minister what the building allows.

## Funeral hymns: the most popular choices in the UK

Most funerals have two or three hymns, and they are the moments when everyone in the room does the same thing: stands, opens the order of service and sings a tune they already know. This guide covers the hymns UK families choose most, where each one sits in a service, and how to settle on two or three that suit the person.

What are the most popular funeral hymns? The hymns UK families ask us for most are The Lord’s My Shepherd, sung to Crimond, for its Psalm 23 words; Abide with Me, Henry Francis Lyte’s hymn of 1847; The Day Thou Gavest, Lord, Is Ended, a gentle last hymn; Dear Lord and Father of Mankind, a prayer for stillness; and Guide Me, O Thou Great Redeemer, for full voice.

## Wedding hymns: the most popular and how to choose

A church wedding usually has two or three hymns, and they are the moments when every guest stands and sings. This guide lists the wedding hymns couples choose most, where each one fits in a Church of England service, and how to pick tunes your guests will sing rather than mumble.

What are the most popular wedding hymns? The hymns couples ask us for most are Love Divine, All Loves Excelling (Charles Wesley, 1747); Jerusalem (William Blake’s words, Hubert Parry’s 1916 tune); Guide Me, O Thou Great Redeemer, sung to Cwm Rhondda; Dear Lord and Father of Mankind; and Be Thou My Vision. On the Church of England’s own wedding planner in 2009, Amazing Grace was the hymn couples chose most.

## Music for a celebration of life

A celebration of life puts remembering the person ahead of mourning them, often with humour and with the music they loved. It may be the funeral itself or a gathering held later. This guide covers the songs families choose, genre by genre, and how to mix live and recorded music.

What music suits a celebration of life? The music the person loved, from any genre, with more room for uplifting songs than a traditional funeral allows. Families choose songs such as Over the Rainbow, What a Wonderful World and Always Look on the Bright Side of Life, a reflective piece such as Time to Say Goodbye, and often one hymn. Three to five pieces is usually enough.

## How to book a choir: steps, costs and the day

You can hire a choir with one message and a deposit. Most people have never done it before, so this guide covers each stage, from the first enquiry to the music on the day. Event planners arranging an awards dinner or a product launch can start with our corporate events page , which shows how a choir fits alongside a pianist or soloist.

How do you hire a choir? Send the date, the venue and the occasion to a choir provider. You get back a written quote naming the ensemble size, the repertoire and the full cost, travel included. A non-refundable deposit of half the fee secures the date, and the singers rehearse before the service. In Greater London a soloist costs £250 and a choir of four £1,150.

## The most popular funeral songs

A funeral song is a piece the room listens to: a solo voice, an instrumental, or a recording played through the speakers. Hymns are the pieces the whole congregation sings, and our guide to popular funeral hymns covers those. This guide covers the songs UK families choose most, who wrote and recorded each one, and whether it works better sung live or played.

What are the most popular funeral songs? In Co-op Funeralcare’s 2025 chart, drawn from a firm that conducts more than 90,000 funerals a year, the top five were Time to Say Goodbye (Andrea Bocelli and Sarah Brightman), My Way (Frank Sinatra), Somewhere Over the Rainbow (Eva Cassidy), You’ll Never Walk Alone and Tina Turner’s The Best. Supermarket Flowers, Wind Beneath My Wings, Abide with Me, We’ll Meet Again and You Raise Me Up completed the top ten.

## Choosing music for a crematorium service

A crematorium service is shorter than a church funeral and runs to a fixed slot, with the next family arriving soon after yours leaves. This guide covers how the music fits that slot, how the chapel’s recorded music is played, what the room sounds like and where live singers help most.

What music can you have at a crematorium? Almost anything. Most services have music at three points: as the coffin comes in, during a moment of reflection or a hymn, and as people leave. Recordings play through the chapel’s system, often Obitus or Wesley Music, with tracks ordered by your funeral director. Live singers and organists are allowed too. A single slot is usually 30 to 40 minutes.

## How to hire a wedding choir

A choir at a wedding leads the hymns and sings while you sign the register. This guide covers what a wedding choir does, how many singers your church or venue needs, what a choir can sing at a church or civil ceremony, and how booking one works, from the first email to the day itself. Our wedding choir hire page has the packages and prices.

How do you hire a choir for a wedding? Send the provider your date, venue and rough guest numbers, ideally six months ahead and sooner for a summer Saturday. Choose the size from the building: four voices suit most parish churches, eight a large one. Agree the hymns and the pieces for the signing of the register, and the choir rehearses in the venue before the ceremony.

## Hiring a UK choir for a destination wedding

Couples who have heard a choir sing in an English church often want that sound at a wedding in Tuscany, the Algarve or Barbados, and assume it is impossible or absurdly expensive. It is a different kind of booking from hiring singers at home. This guide covers what sets the cost, how far ahead you need to commit, the work-permit question few couples raise until it is late, and what changes musically when there is no organ and no stone.

Can you hire a UK choir for a wedding abroad? Yes. Alma Consort, our performing ensemble, takes eight to twenty-four singers from London to weddings in Europe, the Caribbean, the Americas, the Indian Ocean and beyond. The singers rehearse in London, fly out together and rehearse in the building the day before. You get one quote covering the singing, flights and rooms, and the United States needs months of extra notice for visas.

## Wedding ceremony music: processional, register and recessional

A church wedding has five places for music, and three of them shape the day: the processional as the bride walks down the aisle, the music while the couple sign the register, and the recessional as everyone leaves. This guide starts with those three, with the pieces couples choose most, who plays or sings each one and roughly how long it runs. The prelude, hymns and civil ceremonies follow.

What music do you need for a wedding ceremony? Music for five moments: a prelude as guests arrive, often Bach on the organ; a processional for the entrance, such as Clarke’s Trumpet Voluntary ; two or three hymns, such as Love Divine, All Loves Excelling ; a piece during the signing of the register, often Schubert’s Ave Maria ; and a recessional, usually Widor’s Toccata or Mendelssohn’s Wedding March .

## Pairing readings with music at your wedding

A wedding ceremony alternates spoken readings with hymns and choral music, and each piece meets the mood the one before it left. Choose them in pairs and your guests can follow the shape of the service. Choose them one at a time and it can lurch from a quiet sonnet to a full-throated hymn with nothing in between.

How do you pair wedding readings with music? Match each piece to the reading before it. Four church pairings that work: 1 Corinthians 13 with Charles Wesley’s Love Divine, All Loves Excelling (1747); Song of Songs 8:6–7 with Walton’s Set Me as a Seal upon Thine Heart (1938); Ruth 1:16–17 with Duruflé’s Ubi caritas (1960); and Shakespeare’s Sonnet 116 with Lord of All Hopefulness , sung to Slane . A civil ceremony needs secular readings and secular music.

## Planning a corporate or office carol service

A carol service gives a company something a drinks reception can’t: an hour in which the whole office, from new joiners to senior partners, sings the same carols in the same room. This guide covers the date, the venue, the music and readings, a sample running order and the costs, whether the service is for staff in your own atrium or for clients in a City church. Our company carol services page covers booking the choir.

How do you plan a corporate or office carol service? Pick a Tuesday, Wednesday or Thursday in the second or third week of December, then a room: a church, your own atrium or a hotel function room. Book the singers as soon as you have the date. Choose six to eight carols and three to six readings, print the words in a programme, and allow 45 minutes at lunchtime or an hour after work.

## Live choral music for company Christmas parties

When guests walk into a room and hear four voices singing O Come, All Ye Faithful in close harmony, they stop talking for a moment, and then they talk to each other differently. This guide covers the formats that work at a company Christmas party, from roaming carols at arrival to a featured set after dinner, along with the repertoire, the venue, what it costs and when to book.

What live entertainment works at a company Christmas party? Professional carol singers, unamplified, in a format that follows the evening: roaming carols as guests arrive with a drink, quiet close-harmony sets between courses, then a 15–20 minute performance ending in a singalong of Hark! The Herald Angels Sing . They need no stage or sound check. Four singers cost £1,150 for up to two hours, with no VAT added.

## The best Christmas carols for a carol service

Get the carols right and a room of three hundred sings without being asked twice. A good programme sets the congregational favourites that fill a church against the choir pieces that quieten it, and usually finds room for one piece most of the audience has never heard.

Which carols make the best carol service, and how many? Plan six to eight carols for a service of 45 minutes to an hour. Give the congregation three or four it knows, such as Once in Royal David’s City , O Come, All Ye Faithful and Hark! The Herald Angels Sing . Add two or three choir pieces, such as Darke’s In the Bleak Midwinter , and finish with a big congregational carol.

## Best hymns for a Catholic funeral

A Catholic funeral Mass follows the Order of Christian Funerals, and its music belongs at fixed points: the entrance, the psalm, the preparation of the gifts, Communion, the farewell and the procession out. This guide goes through those points, then the hymns and solo pieces families ask us for most, and what to agree with the parish priest.

What are the most popular hymns for a Catholic funeral? Nobody keeps an official count. At the Requiem Masses we sing, families ask most for The Lord’s My Shepherd (Crimond), Be Not Afraid, Here I Am, Lord, Make Me a Channel of Your Peace and Abide with Me. The solo we are asked for most is Schubert’s Ave Maria at Communion, and older families still choose Soul of My Saviour.

Summary: A practical guide to choosing music for a non-religious, secular, or humanist funeral — from popular songs and classical pieces to live performance.
(Shortened to its answer and headings; the page has the full text.)

## Non-religious funeral music

A non-religious funeral may be a humanist ceremony, a civil service led by an independent celebrant, or a celebration of life. The music can come from anywhere, and it needs no organ or church. This guide covers the songs and classical pieces families choose, where each one sits in the service, and when a live singer serves you better than a recording.

What music can you have at a non-religious funeral? Any music you like. Humanist and civil celebrants set no rules, and crematoria play recordings through their own systems or welcome live musicians. Families mix popular songs such as My Way and Time to Say Goodbye, classical pieces such as Elgar’s Nimrod, and sometimes a hymn the person loved. Most services have three or four pieces.

## What to expect from a funeral choir

This guide is for families who have not had a choir at a funeral before. It covers what the singers do during the service, how many you need, what they sing, and what happens on the day, from the time they arrive to the last piece as the coffin leaves. Our funeral choir hire page lists the packages and prices.

What does a funeral choir do? A funeral choir leads the congregation in the hymns, sings up to three pieces of its own, such as Schubert’s Ave Maria or Fauré’s Pie Jesu , and sings or plays as people arrive and leave. Our singers are in the building 45 to 60 minutes early to rehearse. A soloist costs £250, a choir of four £1,150 and a choir of eight £2,000.

## The best choral pieces for a wedding

At a wedding the choir leads the hymns, and it also sings on its own where the ceremony pauses: as guests arrive, during the signing of the register and after the vows. This guide covers the pieces that work best at each point, with composers and dates. For sizes, logistics and costs, see our guide to hiring a wedding choir .

What are the best choral pieces for a wedding? The standards are Schubert’s Ave Maria (1825) and the Bach/Gounod Ave Maria (1859), Franck’s Panis Angelicus (1872), Mozart’s Ave Verum Corpus (1791) and Laudate Dominum (1780), Fauré’s Pie Jesu , the Ubi Caritas of Duruflé (1960) or Ola Gjeilo (1999), and John Rutter’s The Lord Bless You and Keep You (1981).

## Wedding music ideas your guests will remember

Most church weddings follow one musical formula: the organ for the entrance, two hymns, something triumphant on the organ at the end. It works, and our guide to wedding ceremony music walks through it moment by moment. This guide is for couples who want to go further: where the singers stand, which instruments play when, and the one piece your guests won’t expect.

What are some unusual wedding music ideas? Open with one unaccompanied voice. Put a singer in the organ gallery so the sound comes from above and behind. Change the instruments between sections, with strings for the prelude and organ for the entrance. Add one piece nobody expects, such as a folk song or a film theme arranged for choir, or have a song of your own arranged for voices.

## How to plan a memorial service

A memorial service brings together the people who knew someone to remember them, usually some weeks or months after the funeral and without a coffin present. This guide covers when to hold one, the format and venue, a running order you can adapt, and the music.

How do you plan a memorial service? Set a date, usually some weeks or months after the funeral, and book the venue first. Then choose who will lead it and who will speak. A typical service lasts 45 minutes to an hour: music as guests arrive, a welcome, a hymn or song, two or three tributes and readings, a solo or choral piece, a closing hymn, and music as people leave.

## Why Be Thou My Vision is the best wedding hymn

Be Thou My Vision is an Irish hymn sung to the folk tune Slane, and it is one of the hymns couples ask us for most often. The words are a prayer of single-minded devotion, the tune is easy for a congregation to pick up, and it sits well in Anglican, Catholic and non-denominational services.

Is it a good wedding hymn? Yes. On a wedding day a prayer to put one love above everything else reads as a vow, and guests who have never heard Slane are singing it by the second verse. Most couples place it second of three hymns, after the readings or the address, with a brighter hymn to open and close the service.

(Shortened to its answer and headings; the page has the full text.)

## Why Be Thou My Vision is the best funeral hymn

Be Thou My Vision is an Irish hymn sung to the folk tune Slane, and families choose it for funerals in churches and crematoria. The words are a short prayer of trust, and the melody stays in a range most people can manage, so the congregation can keep singing when voices catch.

Is Be Thou My Vision suitable for a funeral? Yes. It is a prayer of trust that makes no promise grief will pass, and its tune, Slane, is easy for a congregation to follow. We suggest it as the last hymn, before the commendation and farewell. It also works as the first hymn, at a church funeral or a crematorium service of 30 to 40 minutes.

## Pop songs on the organ at your wedding

A good church organist can play most of the pop songs couples ask for, but some suit the instrument far better than others. A song with a strong tune and moving chords survives without its drums and electric guitar; a song built on a beat or on one singer’s voice does not. This guide covers the organ on its own: the pop, film and musical-theatre songs our organists play at weddings, where each fits in the service, and how to brief an organist on an arrangement. For pop songs sung by voices, see our guide to pop songs for a wedding choir ; for the classical repertoire, see popular wedding organ music .

Can an organist play pop songs at a wedding? Yes. Most professional organists can arrange a pop song for the organ if you give them a few weeks. Songs with a strong tune and moving harmony work best: Can’t Help Falling in Love (Elvis Presley, 1961), Perfect (Ed Sheeran, 2017), A Thousand Years (Christina Perri, 2011) and Fix You (Coldplay, 2005), which already opens on an organ. Drum-led dance tracks rarely work.

## Lesser-known choral pieces for a wedding

If you have heard Schubert’s Ave Maria at the last four weddings you went to, this guide is for you. It covers choral pieces our singers perform for couples who want something less familiar: Renaissance motets, English cathedral anthems, Romantic works and modern pieces from the last fifty years. Choirs know them well, and most of your guests will hear them for the first time. For the familiar standards ( Ave Maria , Panis Angelicus , Rutter’s blessings), see our guide to the best choral pieces for a wedding .

What are some lesser-known choral pieces for a wedding? Try Palestrina’s Sicut Cervus , Tallis’s If Ye Love Me (1565), Byrd’s Ave Verum Corpus (1605), Brahms’s Geistliches Lied (1856), Stanford’s Beati Quorum Via (published 1905), William Harris’s Faire Is the Heaven (1925), Howells’s Like as the Hart (1941) and Tavener’s The Lamb (1982). Cathedral choirs sing them often; few wedding guests know them.

## Popular wedding organ music

The organ pieces couples book most often at British weddings, in service order: processionals for the walk in, quieter pieces for the signing of the register, and recessionals for the way out. After those come four rarer pieces worth asking your organist for, the pop songs that suit the instrument, and a sample four-piece programme.

What is the most popular wedding organ music? For the walk in, Jeremiah Clarke’s Trumpet Voluntary (c.1700), Pachelbel’s Canon in D and Wagner’s Bridal Chorus (1850). For the signing of the register, Bach’s Jesu, Joy of Man’s Desiring . For the way out, Mendelssohn’s Wedding March (1842) and the Toccata from Widor’s Organ Symphony No. 5 (1879). Couples ask us for these six more than any others.

### The five processionals couples book most
#### Trumpet Voluntary (Jeremiah Clarke, c.1700)
#### Bridal Chorus (Wagner, 1850)
#### Canon in D (Pachelbel, late 17th century)
#### Arrival of the Queen of Sheba (Handel, 1748)
#### Prelude in C from The Well-Tempered Clavier (Bach, BWV 846, 1722)
### Four pieces that suit the register signing
#### Jesu, Joy of Man’s Desiring (Bach, 1723)
#### Air on the G String (Bach, c.1730)
#### Gymnopédie No. 1 (Satie, 1888)
#### Clair de Lune (Debussy, 1905)
### Six recessionals that lift the room
#### Imperial March (Elgar, 1897)
#### Wedding March (Mendelssohn, 1842)
#### Toccata from Symphony No. 5 (Widor, 1879)
#### Hornpipe from Water Music (Handel, 1717)
#### Crown Imperial (Walton, 1937)
#### Toccata in F (Bach, BWV 540)
