## Best Christmas carol singers — what to look for when hiring

Carol singers range from a costumed quartet in a department-store atrium to eight conservatoire graduates in a members’ club, and two quotes for four singers can be hundreds of pounds apart. This guide is for whoever has been asked to book carol singers for an office party, a shop, a hotel lobby, a gala dinner, a charity fundraiser or a residents’ evening. It covers the training to look for, how many voices suit the room, what the fee should include and six questions to ask any provider.

How do you choose the best carol singers? Check that the singers are trained, have sung together, and can move between traditional carols and close-harmony songs such as Winter Wonderland . Match the number to the room: four for an office reception or hotel lobby, six for a busy party, eight for a loud one. Get what the fee includes in writing, and ask whether December costs more.

Summary: Nine Lessons and Carols order of service: the nine readings with Bible references, a worked running order, a service sheet template and a 45-minute outline.
(Shortened to its answer and headings; the page has the full text.)

## Nine Lessons and Carols: order of service and readings

A service of Nine Lessons and Carols is nine readings tracing the Christmas story from Genesis to the first chapter of St John, with a carol after each one. The order was written for a Cambridge chapel in 1918, and it now turns up in parish churches, school chapels, livery halls, and company carol services with no liturgy in them at all. This guide covers where the service came from, what the nine readings are, who reads them, how congregational carols and choir-only pieces are balanced between the lessons, and what you need to organise if you are hiring a choir and an organist into a church you have booked yourself.

The order of service: a processional hymn, usually Once in Royal David’s City ; the Bidding Prayer and the Lord’s Prayer; nine readings running from Genesis 3 to John 1, each followed by a carol or hymn; a collect and the blessing; and a last hymn, at King’s Hark! The Herald Angels Sing , before the organ voluntary. Most services last 55 to 70 minutes.

### Nine Lessons and Carols: the readings
### Order of service
### Service sheet template

Carol-singing quotes are hard to compare: one provider prices per singer, another per set, and some add a December surcharge. This guide sets out what we charge in 2026, what the fee covers and which choices change it. The rate card itself is on our Christmas prices page.

## Planning a charity carol concert

People will pay to sing carols in a church in December, which makes a ticketed carol concert one of the easier fundraisers to sell. The work sits in the arrangements: a church on a date your supporters can reach, a running order that holds the room for an hour, and an appeal placed where the audience is ready to give. We take them in the order an events team meets them, from the first venue enquiry in spring to the collection buckets on the night.

How do you plan a charity carol concert? Book a church for a weekday evening in mid-December, in spring if you can. Plan an hour: six congregational carols, five choir pieces, four short readings and a three-minute appeal two-thirds of the way through. Check that the church’s PRS for Music licence covers your event, give the council a Temporary Event Notice if you sell drinks in an unlicensed building, and price tickets to fill the pews.

## Christmas entertainment for hotels

A hotel at Christmas is already full of people. Guests come down for afternoon tea, drop bags at the desk, wait for a table or stand about with a glass before dinner, and live carol singers give them something to stop for in those minutes. The singers need no stage, no power and no sound check. This guide covers which format suits a lobby, a tea room and a ballroom, how to schedule singers across December, what the choir wears and sings, and what to settle before you sign.

What Christmas entertainment works in a hotel? Live carol singers, unamplified, in three formats. In the lobby, four to six singers roam between the tree, the stairs and the front desk through the arrivals peak. At festive afternoon tea they sing twenty-minute sets, and a pianist can cover the gaps. At a ballroom or private dinner they give one 15–25 minute set ending in a singalong. Four singers cost £1,150 for up to two hours.

## Hosting a residents’ carol event

A carol evening asks less of a building than any other residents’ event. You need mulled wine and a tray of mince pies, and a professional choir sings unaccompanied, so there is no stage to build, no power to run and no sound system to hire. A lobby will do. This guide is for property managers, estate teams, residents’ association committees and care home activity coordinators working out where to hold one, how to shape the evening and what a choir costs.

How do you host a Christmas carol event for residents? Choose a space everyone can reach (the lobby, a courtyard with an indoor fallback, or a care home lounge), put out mulled wine and mince pies, and book a choir for about ninety minutes: two or three sets of carols, then a singalong from printed word sheets. Four unaccompanied singers cost £1,150, and the singing needs no stage, power or entertainment licence.

## When to book Christmas entertainment

From the last week of November, offices, hotels, livery halls and charities all want the same few evenings, and a choir can sing at only one of them. Our diary fills in the order the enquiries arrive. This guide explains which December dates go first, what we need from you to hold one, and why a late enquiry is still worth sending.

When should you book Christmas entertainment? For a December date, book as early as you can. Most years our December dates start to fill by then, and Christmas Eve, Christmas Day and the Thursday and Friday evenings of the first fortnight go first. Late bookings are still welcome: a date booked in November or December costs the same, and we confirm availability within one working day.

## Booking carol singers: agency or direct?

You can book carol singers through an entertainment agency or a booking marketplace, which lists many acts in one place, or go direct to a choir that runs its own diary. Both routes get singers through the door. They differ in what you can find out before you commit and in how much of the price you can see.

Should you book carol singers through an agency or direct? Use an agency or marketplace if you want to compare several acts from one enquiry, or need a band and a photographer from the same place. Book direct with a choir if you want to know who will sing, who directs them and what the fee covers before you pay. Either way, get the line-up and the all-in price in writing.

## How many carol singers do you need?

The ceiling matters more than the guest list. A room with a hard floor and height above it carries four voices further than a carpeted function suite carries eight. Below are the sizes we book most, what each one covers, and the point at which adding voices stops making a difference.

How many carol singers do you need? Four for most rooms: an office reception, a hotel lobby or a church seating up to about 200, at £1,150. Six (£1,600) suits a busier mid-sized room, eight (£2,000) a loud bar or a church seating 400, and twelve (£3,000) a ticketed concert or a congregation of several hundred. A quintet is £1,400. Each price covers up to two hours in Greater London.

## The best carols for four voices

Four singers, one to each part, is where our carol bookings start, and most published carol arrangements were written with a bigger choir in mind. Some pieces gain from the clarity of four voices; others fall apart. This guide sorts the standard repertoire into which is which.

What are the best carols for four voices (SATB)? Carols written or harmonised in plain four parts: Praetorius’s Es ist ein Ros entsprungen (1609), Charles Wood’s harmonisation of Ding Dong! Merrily on High (1924), Holst’s In the Bleak Midwinter (1906), Warlock’s Bethlehem Down (1927), Boris Ord’s Adam Lay Ybounden (1957) and the Sussex Carol . Darke’s In the Bleak Midwinter and the Willcocks descants sound better with six or eight.

## Carols by candlelight

Sung by candlelight, the same carols run slower and quieter than they do under electric light, and the congregation hears them as something closer to a vigil than a concert. Candles also bring practical problems that catch organisers out, most of them about whether your singers can see the music.

What is a carols by candlelight service? A carol service sung with the electric lights low or off and the church lit by candles, usually about an hour of readings and carols on a December afternoon or evening. The best-known public one began in Melbourne in 1938, when the radio announcer Norman Banks gathered about 10,000 people in Alexandra Gardens. In Britain the name covers candlelit church services and Christmas concerts alike.

## Outdoor carol singing

A building gives singers reflections and a ceiling to hold the sound. Outdoors you lose both, and the crowd is usually noisier than the same crowd would be indoors. Carol singing still works in the open air, and we sing at markets and switch-ons every December, but you need more voices and a different plan.

Can carol singers perform outdoors? Yes, with cover from rain and enough voices. Four singers is the minimum for unaccompanied carols in a quiet courtyard; a Christmas market or a lights switch-on needs about eight to carry over the crowd. Stand them against a wall or shop front, and give them somewhere warm between twenty-minute sets. Unamplified live music needs no entertainment licence between 8am and 11pm.

## A cappella Christmas songs for a choir

Not every Christmas booking wants carols. A drinks reception, an office party or a hotel lobby usually wants the songs people associate with December rather than with Advent, and most of those were written for exactly the close-harmony texture a small choir provides. This guide covers what works unaccompanied, and what does not.

Which Christmas songs work a cappella? The close-harmony standards of the 1930s and 1940s: Have Yourself a Merry Little Christmas , The Christmas Song , White Christmas , Winter Wonderland , Let It Snow and Santa Claus Is Comin’ to Town . Their chord changes are strong enough for four voices to carry without a band. Songs that rely on production, such as All I Want for Christmas Is You , lose the most.

## Hiring a choir for a church carol service

Plenty of churches want a proper carol service and no longer have the singers for it. A hired choir fills that gap for one evening, and the arrangement is simpler than most incumbents expect. This guide covers what to book, how it fits with your organist and any choir you already have, and what it costs. If you are ready to book, see our church carol service choir page.

How do you hire a choir for a church carol service? Agree the date and running order with your incumbent, then book singers sized to the congregation. Four lead about 150 people and cost £1,150 in Greater London; eight fill a church of 400 for £2,000. Keep your own organist or add ours for £250. Send the carol list a few weeks ahead, and allow 30 to 45 minutes in the church before the doors open.

## Music for a Christmas drinks reception

A drinks reception is the hardest room a choir sings in, and the Christmas booking we take most often. Guests arrive across an hour, nobody sits down or has come to listen, and the noise climbs as the wine goes round. This guide plans the music around those facts: when to start, where the singers stand, what they sing and how many you need.

What music works at a Christmas drinks reception? Unaccompanied singers who start fifteen minutes before guests arrive, roam while people come in, then gather for one stationary set of three or four pieces at the toast or speech. Close-harmony songs such as Winter Wonderland suit a talking room better than carols. Four singers (£1,150) cover a room of up to about 150; six (£1,600) hold their own at a busy reception.

## Music for a Christmas gala or awards dinner

A seated dinner runs to a fixed order with other people’s speeches in it, so music there depends on timing first and repertoire second. The pieces are short, each one has its moment, and the plan has to survive a starter arriving late. This guide covers the three places music usually goes and how to brief the room.

What music works at a Christmas gala or awards dinner? A sung grace before the meal, by one unaccompanied voice, then pieces of two or three minutes between courses or award categories, cued by the toastmaster. Save the carols and the choir’s best piece for a set once the formal business is done. A soloist for the grace costs £250; carol sets start with four singers at £1,150.

A partners’ dinner takes a sung grace and a short set after the meal. A carol service in a City church wants a choir of eight and an organist, £2,250 together.

## Christmas carol lyrics: the words and what they mean

You can probably sing three verses of half a dozen carols without knowing what all the words mean. The texts are old, several are translations, and a few of the best-known lines mean something different from what they sound like. This guide takes the words of eleven carols in turn: what the puzzling phrases mean, who wrote each text and when.

What do the words of Christmas carols mean? Most carol texts use older senses of everyday words. In “God rest ye merry, gentlemen”, rest means keep, so the line asks God to keep you in good spirits. Welkin , in Charles Wesley’s 1739 original of Hark! The Herald Angels Sing , is the sky. Yon in Silent Night means that one over there, and figgy pudding was the West Country name for a plum pudding.

Summary: The difference between Advent and Christmas carols, which belongs before 25 December, and how to programme a service that sits in the weeks between.
(Shortened to its answer and headings; the page has the full text.)

## Advent carols vs Christmas carols

Advent and Christmas are two seasons with two repertoires, and many December carol services mix them without meaning to. At an office or hotel event nobody will complain. In a church the incumbent may have views, so learn the distinction before you build the programme.

What is the difference between Advent carols and Christmas carols? Advent carols belong to the four weeks before Christmas and look forward to a coming that has not happened yet, usually in restrained, modal music; O Come, O Come, Emmanuel , built on the O Antiphons sung from 17 to 23 December, is the best known. Christmas carols, such as O Come, All Ye Faithful , celebrate the birth as done, and belong from 25 December to Epiphany.

### Two seasons, not one
### The Advent repertoire
#### O Come, O Come, Emmanuel
#### Come, Thou Long Expected Jesus
#### Lo, He Comes with Clouds Descending
#### On Jordan’s Bank and Hills of the North, Rejoice
#### Adam Lay Ybounden

## Choosing funeral singers in London: what to look for

Most families choose funeral singers within a few days, while arranging the rest of the service. This guide covers the training to look for, how many singers suit the venue, what the fee should include and six questions to ask any provider before you book. Our funeral singers page lists what we offer and the prices. The right singers depend partly on the room: a large parish church, a chapel of rest, or one of the crematoria at Hendon, Golders Green, Honor Oak or Kensal Green.

How do you choose a funeral singer in London? Choose trained singers who read music and have sung funerals before, then match the number to the venue: a soloist or four voices for a crematorium chapel, four to six for most parish churches. Ask what the fee includes, who speaks to the funeral director, and who replaces a singer who falls ill on the morning.

## Comparing wedding choirs in London: what to look for

London gives couples more choice of wedding choir than most cities: graduates of the Royal Academy of Music, the Royal College of Music, the Guildhall School and Trinity Laban, parish choirs, and agency listings on Encore, Alive Network and PopTop, where very different singers appear side by side at similar prices. This guide covers the training to look for, how to match the choir to the church, what the fee should include, and seven questions to ask any provider before you book. For the packages themselves, see our wedding choir hire page.

How do you choose a wedding choir in London? Check the singers’ training first, then match the number of voices to the building: four suit most parish churches, six to eight a large one. Ask to hear a recording from a real service and get what the fee includes in writing.

Summary: Ubi Caritas is one of the few sacred texts whose subject is love. Why Ola Gjeilo's setting suits a wedding, where to place it, and how many singers it needs.
(Shortened to its answer and headings; the page has the full text.)

## Ubi Caritas at a wedding — Ola Gjeilo’s setting

Most wedding music is about love by association. Ubi Caritas is about love outright: the Latin says that where charity and love are, God is there. Ola Gjeilo’s setting is the modern choral piece couples ask us for most, and the first one we suggest when a couple has run out of ideas for the register signing.

What does Ubi Caritas mean? Ubi caritas et amor, Deus ibi est is Latin for “Where charity and love are, God is there.” It is the refrain of a chant attributed to Paulinus of Aquileia around 796, sung for centuries on Maundy Thursday during the washing of feet. Maurice Duruflé set it in 1960, and Ola Gjeilo’s unaccompanied setting, published by Walton Music, is the one most couples know.

Summary: A humanist wedding is wholly non-religious. The secular choral repertoire a choir can sing at one, where to place it, and the pieces that catch couples out.
(Shortened to its answer and headings; the page has the full text.)

## Choral music for a humanist wedding

A humanist wedding has no religious content, and most wedding choral music is sacred. Take away the Ave Marias, Panis Angelicus and the settings of Ubi Caritas, and couples assume a choir has nothing left to sing. What remains is the secular part-song tradition: Stanford, Elgar, Vaughan Williams, Lauridsen, Whitacre, and four centuries of choral music about love, weather and landscape. Church weddings use hymn books instead, so few couples have heard any of it at a wedding.

What music can you have at a humanist wedding? Any music without religious words, so no hymns, prayers or sung Ave Marias. A choir can sing English part-songs such as Stanford’s The Blue Bird (1910), folk songs such as The Water Is Wide , Renaissance madrigals, Lauridsen’s Dirait-on , Whitacre’s The Seal Lullaby and pop songs with published choral arrangements. In England and Wales no registrar checks the programme, because the humanist ceremony is not the legal marriage.

## It Is Well With My Soul: the words, the story and its place at a funeral

Horatio Spafford wrote It Is Well With My Soul in 1873, weeks after his four daughters drowned in the Atlantic. Families who know the story choose it for a funeral because the man who wrote “whatever my lot” had lost more than most people in the room.

Why is It Is Well With My Soul sung at funerals? Its words hold grief and trust together: the first verse names “sorrows like sea billows” and still ends “it is well with my soul”. The refrain repeats one short phrase, so a congregation that has never sung the hymn can join in by the second verse.

Source: https://londonchoralservice.com/music-guides/love-divine-all-loves-excelling.html
Summary: Love Divine, All Loves Excelling: Wesley's words of 1747, the tunes Blaenwern and Hyfrydol, and its place at funerals and weddings. Singers from £250.
(Shortened to its answer and headings; the page has the full text.)

## Love Divine, All Loves Excelling: words, tunes and where to sing it

Charles Wesley’s Love Divine is one of the few hymns families choose for weddings and funerals alike. It was sung at the wedding of the Prince of Wales and Lady Diana Spencer in 1981 and at the state funeral of Queen Elizabeth II in 2022, and its last line, “lost in wonder, love, and praise”, suits a thanksgiving for a life.

What tune is Love Divine sung to? In Britain, usually Blaenwern, a Welsh tune by William Penfro Rowlands from the time of the 1904–05 revival. Some churches sing it to Hyfrydol, an older Welsh tune by Rowland Prichard, or to John Stainer’s tune Love Divine. Tell the organist which one you want, because the congregation will sing whichever tune the organ plays.

## Memorial service songs and hymns

A memorial service usually comes weeks or months after the funeral, without a coffin, and families plan it with more time. The music can give thanks for a life as well as mourn it. This guide lists the hymns and songs families choose for memorials, the uplifting ones, pieces for a mother or father, and which to sing live.

What are good songs and hymns for a memorial service? In church, families choose hymns of thanks: Love Divine, All Loves Excelling, Jerusalem, Guide Me, O Thou Great Redeemer and Thine Be the Glory. For music the room listens to, Time to Say Goodbye, You Raise Me Up and What a Wonderful World come up most, with Fauré’s Pie Jesu and Handel’s He Shall Feed His Flock when a soloist sings live.

Summary: The Lord's My Shepherd: the 1650 words of Psalm 23, the tune Crimond, and where the hymn sits in a funeral. Hear our singers, then book from £250.
(Shortened to its answer and headings; the page has the full text.)

## The Lord’s My Shepherd: the words, the tune Crimond and its place at a funeral

The Lord’s My Shepherd and Abide With Me are the two hymns families ask us for most at funerals. It is Psalm 23 in verse, and many people who have not been to church in years can still sing the first verse from memory.

What tune is The Lord’s My Shepherd sung to? Crimond, a Scottish tune first published in 1872 and usually credited to Jessie Seymour Irvine. The words come from the Scottish Psalter of 1650. Some churches use Brother James’s Air instead, and Howard Goodall’s setting from The Vicar of Dibley is a separate piece for a choir or soloist to sing.
